James Dell Talarico ( TAL-ə-REE-koh, born May 17, 1989) is an American politician and educator who is the United States senator-elect from Texas. A member of the Democratic Party, he has served since 2018 as a member of the Texas House of Representatives.
Born in Round Rock, Texas, Talarico taught sixth grade language arts at Rhodes Middle School in West San Antonio, Texas from 2011 to 2013. He is a graduate of the University of Texas at Austin (UT) and earned his Master of Education at Harvard University. He also served as an executive director for an education nonprofit. He is currently serving out his fourth term in the Texas House of Representatives, having first been elected in 2018. While serving in the Texas House, Talarico started to pursue a Master of Divinity at Austin Presbyterian Theological Seminary.
Talarico has been described as a populist influenced by Christian social teaching. In 2025, he announced his candidacy for the U.S. Senate election in 2026. He defeated U.S. Representative Jasmine Crockett in the Democratic primary and Republican nominee Ken Paxton in the general election. He is the first Democrat to win a U.S. Senate election in Texas since 1988.

Troy Dale Jackson (born June 26, 1968) is an American politician and former logger who is the United States senator-elect from Maine. A member of the Democratic Party, he served in the Maine Senate from 2008 to 2014 and from 2016 to 2024, representing parts of northern Aroostook County. He was the Senate president from 2018 to 2024.
Jackson grew up in Allagash, Maine, and worked as a logger before entering politics. He first served in the Maine House of Representatives from 2002 to 2008, initially as an independent before joining the Democratic Party. He became involved in politics after helping lead a 1998 blockade by Maine loggers protesting the employment of Canadian workers in the state's logging industry. He served as Senate majority leader from 2013 to 2014 and minority leader from 2016 to 2018.
As Senate president, Jackson pursued a populist agenda focused on labor rights, health care and economic issues. His legislative accomplishments included expanding access to prescription drugs, establishing universal free school meals and increasing child care assistance. After an unsuccessful campaign for governor in 2026, he became the Democratic nominee for the U.S. Senate following a Democratic Nominating Convention that occurred after the withdrawal of former nominee Graham Platner and defeated incumbent Republican Susan Collins in the November general election, becoming the first Democrat to represent Maine in the Senate since George J.
